data.metaTitle: How the data is built — MusiGraph
data.metaDescription: MusiGraph data methodology: Auto mode, precedence and deduplication across Wikidata, Wikipedia, DBpedia, MusicBrainz and Discogs, API limits and licenses.
data.title: How the data is built
data.intro: MusiGraph queries open, linked sources in real time. Auto mode is the default: Wikidata is the core (identity, base data and identifiers) with automatic failover to QLever, and the result is enriched with Wikipedia, DBpedia, MusicBrainz and Discogs. Every piece of data keeps its origin and is labelled with a source badge.

flow.title: Data flow in Auto mode
flow.caption: The Wikidata core is essential and answers first; enrichment sources are queried in parallel, never block the profile, and each one reports its status in the final merge.
flow.diagramTitle: MusiGraph data flow in Auto mode
flow.diagramDesc: The UI calls /api/sparql, which validates and caches the request; the Auto orchestrator queries Wikidata with failover to QLever and, in parallel, Wikipedia, DBpedia, MusicBrainz and Discogs; the result is merged with provenance and feeds the profile tabs.

autoRules.title: Auto mode rules
autoRules.intro: The orchestrator combines sources field by field, deduplicates rows and keeps the origin of every piece of data. These are the rules it applies.
autoRules.caption: Field precedence rules in Auto mode.

rows.order: Wikidata label in the UI language; if missing, a multilingual fallback label.
Wikipedia in the UI language → DBpedia ES (Spanish UI only) → short Wikidata description.
Wikidata P18 image, served as a thumbnail; no further fallbacks today.
MusicBrainz → Wikidata → Discogs, backfilling empty fields (date, label, genre and type).
Union of Wikidata and curated MusicBrainz genres, deduplicated; folksonomy tags are discarded.
Wikidata P737 and P1066 + real MusicBrainz relations (teacher, tribute), with their relation type.
Wikidata works with multiple performers (P175) + MusicBrainz collaboration relations.
Genre similarity is labelled as a suggestion; it is never presented as a verified influence.

autoRules.dedupe: Discographies are deduplicated with two keys: the Wikidata P436 identifier ↔ MusicBrainz release-group as the strong key and, failing that, normalised title (no accents, lowercase) plus year.
autoRules.statuses: Provenance badges show each source's outcome: ok, empty, error, timeout or skipped. Enrichment sources are disposable: if one fails, the profile still renders and only its status is flagged.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: What each source contributes, through which endpoint and under which license.

wikidata.role: Artist identity (QID), per-language labels, dates, country, genres, instruments, partial discography, influences (P737/P1066), collaborations and external identifiers (MusicBrainz, Discogs, Spotify, Last.fm, AllMusic).

qlever.role: The same Wikidata database served by QLever. It kicks in as automatic failover when the core fails or times out, and is also available as an explicit source in the selector.

wikipedia.role: Biography in the UI language, from the artist's linked article (sitelink). Shown with attribution and a link to the original article.

dbpedia.role: Spanish abstract as a biography fallback. Also available as an explicit provider for search and traits.

musicbrainz.role: Discography (release groups: albums, singles and EPs) with date and type; curated genres; real artist relations: member of band, collaboration, teacher and tribute.
musicbrainz.license: MusicBrainz data license (core in the public domain)

discogs.role: Releases (up to 100 per artist) with year, label and format; artist identity search when there is no Discogs ID.

limits.title: Limits and resilience
limits.intro: Public quotas for every API and how MusiGraph mitigates them.
limits.caption: Public limits for each source and the mitigations applied in MusiGraph.

rows.limit: ≈60 s of processing per minute and 5 parallel queries per IP.
rows.mitigation: 1 h server cache and 10 min client cache; 12 s timeout with failover to QLever; 2–3 queries per view.

rows.limit: Community trial endpoint, no service guarantee.
rows.mitigation: Only used as failover or explicit source; 8 s timeout.
Light queries and batched enrichment; aggregates are never trusted; 6 s timeout.

rows.limit: Public read API, no strict quota.
rows.mitigation: 6 s timeout and 6 h cache per language and title.
Queue with 1.1 s spacing and a dedicated User-Agent; 24 h cache; never blocks the profile.
Server-only token; 24 h cache; the source disables itself without a token.

v2.title: WDQS v2 migration
v2.body: Wikidata's v2 endpoints (query-next.wikidata.org) open to the community in November 2026 and the current ones (Blazegraph) will start degrading in February 2027. QLever already works as failover and as an explicit selector option, and every query is written to run on both engines: no label service on QLever (OPTIONAL/COALESCE blocks) and strict xsd:dateTime dates. The endpoint is switchable through server configuration, with no code changes, so the cutover and rollback happen when the v2 endpoints go public.
